strengths: Strong empirical results with significant improvements on challenging real-world data (2.7-16.7x on LaMAR HGE, particularly on short sequences which are practically important)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three diverse datasets with detailed ablation studies on encoder architectures, grid resolution, and component contributions
Clear practical value: improved generalization to new environments and better scalability compared to prior work requiring per-environment network training
Well-motivated problem identification addressing specific limitations of F3Loc with clearly articulated solutions
Excellent supplementary materials with qualitative visualizations (posterior evolution, observation likelihoods) and additional analyses demonstrating thorough evaluation
Solid technical soundness with proper probabilistic formulation, correct histogram filtering integration, and appropriate use of Laplace distributions for robustness
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core contributions are primarily engineering-driven (replacing custom depth network with pre-trained model, adding standard uncertainty estimation). Both components exist in prior work, and integration is straightforward.

Critical absence of uncertainty calibration analysis: no reliability diagrams, ECE metrics, or empirical demonstration that predicted uncertainties correlate with prediction errors—fundamental for a paper centered on uncertainty

Unconventional and unjustified training procedure using only GT depth at GT pose (Eq. 5) without discussion of potential distribution mismatch between training and inference or comparison to standard depth estimation training

Overstated generalization claims: method requires per-dataset training (Table 1), not true zero-shot. Zero-shot performance on LaMAR CAB limited (50% SR@1m). 'Out-of-the-box' framing in abstract is misleading.

Missing key ablations and analyses: no Laplace vs. Gaussian empirical comparison despite justification claims, limited failure mode analysis, no sensitivity studies for uncertainty hyperparameters, and minimal guidance on when uncertainty estimation is beneficial

Computational overhead concerns: significantly slower than F3Loc per-frame (~0.88-0.89s vs ~0.8s on LaMAR), with argument that shorter convergence offsets costs being somewhat hand-wavy and dataset-dependent

Incomplete uncertainty analysis: on single-frame localization, uncertainty provides minimal benefit on Gibson(t)/Structured3D (Table 5), suggesting domain-specific utility not thoroughly characterized
Statistical rigor lacking: no confidence intervals, significance tests, or discussion of noise margins despite some improvements being modest with small test sample sizes (N=11 for LaMAR HGE T=100)

strengths: Strong empirical results with 2.7-16.7× improvements on real-world datasets
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets with extensive ablations
Practical approach addressing real deployment limitations of prior work (F3Loc)
Well-motivated problem identification around uncertainty modeling and dataset-specific training
Detailed supplementary material with generalization studies and efficiency analysis
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily combines F3Loc with better encoder (Depth Anything V2) and Laplace uncertainty prediction
Unclear contribution attribution: Table 5 shows uncertainty provides minimal benefit on synthetic data; encoder choice dominates (Table 6)
Insufficient uncertainty evaluation: no calibration analysis, uncertainty-error correlation, or information-theoretic metrics
Questionable baseline: F3Loc trained by authors shows suspiciously low performance on LaMAR; unclear if this reflects method limitations or poor tuning
Heavy dependence on recent SOTA model (Depth Anything V2 from 2024) rather than methodological innovation
Missing ablations: no comparison of alternative uncertainty quantification methods or isolation of individual component contributions
Computational cost trade-off inadequately addressed: 12× slower feature extraction, 300× slower matching vs. F3Loc
Generalization concerns: cross-domain results (Tables 7-8) show significant fine-tuning needed; robustness to camera variations not evaluated

strengths: Dramatic empirical improvements: 2.7-16.7× better than SOTA on LaMAR HGE, especially on challenging short sequences (15 frames)
Comprehensive evaluation across multiple datasets (Gibson, LaMAR, Structured3D) with both synthetic and real-world data
Thorough ablation studies demonstrating individual contributions of pre-trained models and uncertainty modeling
Addresses real practical limitations of F3Loc: lack of uncertainty modeling and per-environment training requirement
Well-designed probabilistic model with proper Bayesian formulation and justified design choices (Laplace distribution)
Practical benefits: enables off-the-shelf pre-trained models, better generalization, no per-dataset retraining
Excellent presentation with clear figures, comprehensive supplementary material, and sound technical writing
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: primarily an engineering contribution combining existing techniques (pre-trained networks, Laplace uncertainty, histogram filtering) rather than novel methods
Uncertainty modeling lacks rigorous analysis: no calibration studies, no investigation of when/where uncertainty helps, single-frame results show minimal benefit contradicting core motivation
Generalization claims overstated: cross-domain results require fine-tuning (e.g., 200 fine-tuning images for optimal performance), not truly zero-shot despite pre-training
Real-world evaluation limited to single building (LaMAR HGE): only one real building tested, CAB results on same campus, no diverse environments
Computational cost trade-off: ~1s/frame vs F3Loc's ~0.8s not fully justified, matching stage still dominates (0.88s vs 0.18s)
Insufficient technical details: GT depth computation during training vague, independence assumption in observation model (Eq. 1) not justified, network output compatibility unclear
Limited baseline comparisons: LaLaLoc/LaLaLoc++/PF-Net not directly compared, LASER results only from prior work reports
Method requires gravity direction from sensors (IMU access needed), limiting applicability to devices without orientation sensors

strengths: Strong experimental results with substantial improvements over prior art (2.7× on long sequences, 42.2× on short sequences on challenging real-world LaMAR dataset)
Comprehensive evaluation including multiple datasets, thorough ablations, single-frame and sequential analysis, and cross-domain generalization tests
Principled technical approach with well-justified design choices (Laplace distributions for efficiency and robustness, proper Bayesian formulation, appropriate training loss)
Practical system design that leverages off-the-shelf pre-trained models, improving generalization and reducing per-environment training burden
Clear, well-written presentation with informative visualizations and detailed appendix supporting reproducibility
Addresses real limitations of prior work (F3Loc) with concrete solutions that demonstrate practical value
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty - primarily combines existing techniques (uncertainty estimation for depth, pre-trained models) in a straightforward manner without fundamental new insights or methodology

Experimental concerns regarding fairness of baseline comparison: F3Loc mono shows unusually poor performance on LaMAR (36.4% vs near-perfect on Gibson), and no official F3Loc model exists for LaMAR, raising questions about training setup and fair comparison

Insufficient analysis of uncertainty quality and calibration - no uncertainty calibration metrics (ECE, reliability diagrams), and ablation comparing Laplace vs. Gaussian limited to sequence lengths rather than uncertainty calibration

Substantial contribution from post-processing optimization (16 percentage point improvement on short sequences) suggests base method may not be fully optimized and reduces impact of core methodological contributions
Incomplete uncertainty analysis - limited investigation into when uncertainty modeling helps vs. hurts, no comparison with alternative uncertainty quantification approaches for depth
Limited real-world validation with only one real-world dataset (LaMAR with two variants); cross-domain generalization shows notable performance drops without fine-tuning

Computational cost and scalability concerns not thoroughly addressed - matching time increases substantially on large floorplans, post-processing adds 0.96s overhead, efficiency analysis limited to relatively simple scenes
Method requires gravity direction and camera intrinsics as input, adding practical constraints; independence assumption in Eq. 1 for neighboring rays may not hold but impact not discussed

strengths: Well-motivated practical improvements addressing clear limitations of F3Loc (lack of uncertainty modeling and per-dataset depth network training)
Comprehensive and thorough experimental evaluation across multiple datasets (Gibson, LaMAR HGE, LaMAR CAB) with extensive ablations (encoders, grid resolution, uncertainty distributions)
Strong quantitative results with 42.2× improvement on 15-frame LaMAR HGE sequences; good cross-domain generalization demonstrated
Well-justified technical choices (Laplace distribution for heavier tails, closed-form likelihood computation), sound mathematical formulation of loss function
Good reproducibility with promised code release, detailed implementation details, and clear training procedures
Practical modularity: method works with arbitrary pre-trained depth models without retraining, demonstrated with multiple encoder variants
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: straightforward application of well-established uncertainty estimation techniques to floorplan localization; core components (depth uncertainty, histogram filtering) are from prior work

Questionable baseline comparison fairness: F3Loc shows extreme performance degradation on LaMAR (1.2% success rate), raising questions about proper implementation or dataset compatibility; missing comparison to F3Loc fusion with Depth Anything v2 encoder

Insufficient uncertainty analysis: no calibration metrics (reliability diagrams, ECE); limited investigation into when/why uncertainty helps more on LaMAR than Gibson; improvements on single-frame localization minimal, suggesting benefits concentrate in sequential fusion

Post-processing optimization contributes substantially to results (16 percentage points on Gibson T=15) yet is somewhat orthogonal to main contributions; inconsistent reporting of with/without post-processing across tables obscures true contribution attribution

Inadequately discussed computational cost trade-offs: Depth Anything v2 increases runtime 6× over F3Loc on Gibson; on LaMAR all methods require ~1 second per frame; post-processing adds 0.96s per sequence
Claim of 'no per-dataset training' is misleading: masked attention mechanism still requires per-dataset training; cross-domain results require fine-tuning for good performance
Limited failure case analysis and discussion of fundamental limitations: single-frame LaMAR performance gap (17.1% vs. 49.2% with GT depth) indicates depth remains significant bottleneck
Key design choice justifications lacking: Laplace vs. Gaussian relegated to appendix; masked attention modifications from F3Loc unclear; no exploration of using depth models' native uncertainty

strengths: Strong experimental results with comprehensive evaluation across multiple datasets (Gibson, LaMAR) and extensive ablation studies examining different encoders, grid resolutions, and observation frequencies
Well-motivated problem addressing genuine limitations of F3Loc: lack of uncertainty modeling and environment-specific depth network training requirements
Technically sound methodology with principled probabilistic formulation using Laplace distributions and clear justification for design choices
Particularly strong performance on short sequences (42.2× improvement on 15-frame sequences), which has practical importance for time-critical localization
Thorough evaluation including single-frame analysis, cross-dataset generalization, runtime analysis, and detailed ablations showing contribution of each component
Well-written paper with clear presentation, informative visualizations, and commitment to reproducibility with promised code release
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: primarily combines existing ideas (pre-trained depth models + Laplace uncertainty estimation); both components are incremental adaptations of prior work rather than fundamental innovations

Overstated generalization claims: despite framing around 'off-the-shelf pre-trained models,' the method still requires per-dataset training, as evidenced by substantial performance gaps when applied to unseen datasets without fine-tuning (Tables 4, 7, 8)

Confounded experimental improvements make it difficult to isolate the contribution: improvements come from (a) full dataset vs. cropped version used in original F3Loc, (b) better pre-trained models, (c) post-processing optimization, and (d) the proposed method

Uncertainty quality not validated: no analysis of uncertainty calibration, correlation with actual prediction errors, or whether predicted uncertainties are well-calibrated; Table 11 shows marginal Laplacian vs. Gaussian differences, suggesting theoretical justification is post-hoc

Single-frame results show minimal uncertainty benefits (Table 6: Gibson MAE 0.25 vs 0.25, LaMAR 2.02 vs 2.08), indicating most gains come from temporal fusion rather than improved depth estimation, questioning the value of uncertainty modeling innovation

Post-processing (Section 3.8) is necessary for competitive results but appears somewhat ad-hoc; unclear whether this should be considered part of the core method and it confounds contribution attribution

Ground truth annotation for LaMAR relies on manual alignment with 4 point pairs and affine transformation; while consistency checks are mentioned, independent validation would strengthen the reliability of reported large improvements
Independence assumption in likelihood formulation (Eq. 1) across rays lacks justification despite adjacent rays being highly correlated; no discussion of how this assumption impacts results
